2015_079_050515mtg.paragraph: Board of Education packet for the Troy School District regular meeting of May 5, 2015, held at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Contents run from recognitions and the March 2015 Treasurer's Report through four board policies, reviews of special education and English Language Development, and business items 8.A through 8.K. The heaviest actions are bond-funded: $4,642,337.00 in mechanical, electrical and site contracts for Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools, and a $1,940,978.41 technology package recommended by Convergent Technology Partners. Item 8.J presents the Oakland Schools proposed 2015-2016 budgets, $292.2 million in revenue against $300.0 million in expenditures, which item 8.K supports under Section 624 of the Revised School Code.
2015_079_050515mtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, 7:00 p.m., May 5, 2015, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions**
Schroeder Elementary partners with IA-West and buildOn to build a school in Haiti. Thirteen Outstanding Support Staff nominees are honored, with Teri Brune of Boulan Park Middle School named Employee of the Year. Retirees receive clocks from President Nancy Philippart. A resolution supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 4-8, 2015. Sodexo General Manager Gayle Moran presents $2,500 to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence and a $1,000 culinary arts scholarship.

**Consent agenda and policies**
Minutes of the April 14, 2015 special meeting, closed session and regular meeting and the April 21 workshop; the Treasurer's Report; and second reading and adoption of B-1210 Closed Session, B-1301 Agenda Format, B-1401 Minutes, and J-2012 Anti-Bullying.

**Personnel (6.A)**
Ratification of the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA contract. Tentative agreement reached April 22, 2015; TEA membership ratified April 30, 2015; the agreement extends the contract through June 30, 2016, with step improvements on the existing 14-step salary schedule, a board-paid annuity, health insurance adjustments as permitted under Public Act 152, and continuation of two additional instruction days.

**Curriculum (7.A-7.D)**
Special Ed Review by Donna Tinberg of Thayer-North Educational Consulting LLC, presented by Kathy Jagels. ELD Program Review by Mary Haezebrouck, Tammy DiPonio and Anne Mull reports 1,655 English Learners (1,171 elementary, 484 secondary) against 1,120 in June 2014, with twelve recommendations from consultant Jo Gusman. ELD materials recommendation of National Geographic REACH Levels A-C and Grammar Gallery. Formal adoption of the K-5 elementary block schedule pilot begun in 2013-2014.

**Business awards (8.A-8.I)**

| Item | Party | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Audit services | Yeo & Yeo, P.C. | not to exceed $48,650 (2014-2015); $50,400.00 (2015-2016); $52,150.00 (2016-2017) |
| Environmental testing | Nova Environmental | $42,920.00 |
| Video surveillance | SimplexGrinnell | $325,507.00 |
| 3,800 iPad Air tablets | Apple, Inc. | $1,437,196.00 |
| 3,800 iPad covers | CDWG | $87,400.00 |
| Power supplies | SEHI, Inc. | $37,787.41 |
| Troy High mechanical | ThermalNetics | $327,500.00 |
| 2,400 Airwatch MDM licenses | CDWG | $53,088.00 |
| Boulan/Larson mechanical, electrical, site | Advanced Building Group, Ecker Mechanical, Metro Electric, Nagle Paving | $4,642,337.00 |

All are charged to the 2014 Capital Projects Fund except the audit (General Fund) and the Airwatch licenses (2014-2015 General Fund).

**Oakland Schools budget (8.J, 8.K)**
Rick West presents the Oakland Intermediate School District proposed 2015-2016 budgets, required under Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624): submission by May 1, constituent resolution by June 1. Total revenue is $292.2 million, led by $170.8 million in property tax; total expenditures $300.0 million, led by $132.6 million in transfers to LEAs and other funds. Annual property tax collection declined 23.4% from FY 2008 to FY 2015, a cumulative $244.4 million against a $216.9 million base-year levy. Item 8.K expresses support solely to comply with Section 624.

**Other (10.A, 10.B)**
Bond Projects Update from Ron Curtis, Senior Project Manager, Barton Malow, covering Troy High additions and Boulan Park and Larson office additions completing about December 2015. First reading of the board policy on Compensation and Expenses, which sets board member compensation at $100 per annum.

**Treasurer's Report, March 2015**
Total check disbursements $3,687,254.41; ACH debits $68,882.78; outgoing wire transfers $2,807,364.19; P-Card purchases $175,140.37; prior period void disbursements $(28,418.93); total disbursements in period $6,710,222.82. General Fund balance was $20,458,563 at March 31, 2015.
2015_079_050515mtg.verbose:
Agenda and supporting packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 7:00 p.m., May 5, 2015, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us.

**Recognitions.** Schroeder Elementary's partnership with IA-West and buildOn is building a school in Haiti after earlier schools in Nicaragua and Nepal. Thirteen 2014-2015 Outstanding Support Staff nominees are recognized, with Teri Brune of Boulan Park Middle School named Employee of the Year and forwarded for the county-wide Betty Campion Award. Retirees receive clocks from Board President Nancy Philippart with names read by Larry Lobert; among them Jerry Cottone (Principal, Leonard, 39 years), Robert Bevier (Counselor, Boulan Park, 38) and Jan Keeling (Assistant Superintendent Elementary Instruction, 37 1/2). A resolution supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 4-8, 2015. Sodexo General Manager Gayle Moran presents $2,500 to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, accepted by TFEE Grant Chair Teri Brune, plus a $1,000 culinary arts scholarship.

**Consent agenda and April minutes.** Items A-F cover minutes of the April 14, 2015 special board meeting, closed session and regular meeting and the April 21 workshop; the Treasurer's Report; and second reading of B-1210, B-1301, B-1401 and J-2012. At the April 14 special meeting Resolution 15-031 approved a closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), 5-0, with Clark Hill counsel John Gierak and Barb Ruga present. At the April 14 regular meeting, Resolution 15-033 awarded Smith Middle School and Niles remodeling bids totaling $308,486.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and Resolution 15-034 awarded data storage and backup to EMC/Presidio for $469,750.00. Rick West reported the 2006 bond refunding saved $3.9 million over the next 10 years, and Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants reported 52 fewer students than projected for 2014/2015.

**Treasurer's Report, March 2015.** Memo from Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, dated May 5, 2015. Check disbursements: General Fund (101) $2,946,843.55, Grant Fund (120) $19,072.44, Special Education Fund (122) $169,667.05, total general fund $3,135,583.04; Food Service (520) $91,894.38, Troy Career Center (529) $24,779.59, Community Education (530) $42,731.20, Facilities Rental (535) $341.85, total special revenue $159,747.02; Building & Site (414) $266,701.08, Student Activity (700, 701) $124,223.27, Memorial Scholarship (750) $1,000.00, total other funds $391,924.35; total check disbursements $3,687,254.41. ACH debits $68,882.78, outgoing wire transfers $2,807,364.19, P-Card purchases $175,140.37, prior period void disbursements $(28,418.93), total disbursements in period $6,710,222.82.

**Budget reports, March year to date, fiscal 2015.** General Fund revenue: budget $142,706,181, actual $95,587,948, uncollected $47,118,233 (33.02%). Expenditures: budget $143,627,633, actual $96,376,034, encumbered $2,819,449, available $44,432,150 (30.94%); total instruction $92,952,882 against $60,556,993. Excess revenue over expenditures $(921,452); fund balance $21,380,015 at March 1 and $20,458,563 at March 31, 2015. Consolidated special revenue funds: revenue $8,635,670 budget and $6,324,137 actual; expenditures $7,840,568 and $5,358,228; excess $795,102; fund balance $3,541,661 to $4,336,763. Food Service ends at $1,758,788, Troy Career Center $1,973,956, Adult & Community Education $357,030, Facilities Rental $246,989. Debt service funds show property taxes of $16,120,449 against a $15,456,298 budget, proceeds from bond refunding of $37,504,183, total revenue $54,469,645, other expenditures $38,262,512, total expenditures $42,325,740, excess $(330,705), and fund balance from $853,935 to $523,230. Capital projects funds (499, 414) show capital outlay of $13,431,799 and fund balance of $51,620,195; the internal service fund (681) ends at $25,318.

**Check register.** A Pentamation ACCTPA21 "Check Register - By Fund" run 04/29/2015 for accounting period 10/15, cash account A1003. Printed fund totals: 101 $2,946,843.55; 120 $19,072.44; 122 $169,667.05; 414 (2014 Cap Proj - Series 1) $266,701.08; 520 $91,894.38; 529 $24,779.59; 530 $42,731.20; 535 $341.85; 700 $121,992.22; 701 $2,231.05; 750 $1,000.00; total report $3,687,254.41. Larger payments include Enviro Clean Services $278,541.79 (custodial), Constellation Energy $169,516.62, SEHI Computer Products $151,262.26, First Group America $111,538.05 plus $86,933.72 in special education transportation, MPSERS wires of $911,704.39 and $527,086.32, Safe Ed LLC $30,433.57, Troy Education Association Scholarship $22,160.00 for 277 students at $80 each, Clark Hill PLC $18,756.25 and The Hanover Research $18,000.00.

**Policies.** B-1210 Closed Sessions requires five affirmative roll call votes except under subsections 1, 2 and 3, lists seven permitted purposes, and requires closed-session minutes to be destroyed one year and one day after approval, disclosable only under Section 10, 11 or 13 of Act No. 267, Public Acts 1976; adopted April 8, 1975, last revised April 15, 2003. B-1301 sets the agenda order; last revised April 20, 2010. B-1401 Minutes requires proposed minutes available within eight business days and approved minutes within five, under the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, Act No. 442, PA 1976; adopted April 8, 1975, last revised April 17, 2012. J-2012 Anti-Bullying names the superintendent as Responsible School Official and cites Section 219a of the Michigan Penal Code, MCL 750.219a; adopted June 5, 2012, revised May 6, 2014.

**Personnel and curriculum.** Item 6.A ratifies the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA agreement reached April 22, 2015 and ratified by TEA membership April 30, 2015, extending the contract through June 30, 2016 with steps on the existing 14-step salary schedule, a board-paid annuity, health insurance adjustments under Public Act 152, and two additional instruction days; the resolution covers April 30, 2014 through June 30, 2016. The Special Ed Review by Donna Tinberg of Thayer-North Educational Consulting LLC, presented by Kathy Jagels, recommends linking the Student Assistance Process to a Multi-Tiered System of Supports and less categorical service delivery. The ELD Program Review reports 1,655 current English Learners (1,171 elementary, 484 secondary) versus 1,120 in June 2014, an increase of 535; of 287 students enrolled between 9/3/2014 and 1/22/15, 145 or 50.52% were ELs. Special education counts are 1,078 with speech and language (468 elementary, 610 secondary) and 831 without (278, 553). Consultant Jo Gusman's twelve recommendations include renaming ESL to ELD, an ELD Administrator partly funded by Title III, more ELD Specialists against a current ratio of 1/161 to 1/204, and WIDA-trained assessors. Item 7.C, by Christin Silagy and Danielle Andresen, notes Michigan joined WIDA in January 2013 with assessment beginning September 2013, cites 80+ languages district-wide, and recommends National Geographic REACH Levels A-C and Grammar Gallery by Dr. Roberta Stathis and Patrice Gotsch. Item 7.D formalizes the K-5 specials block schedule pilot begun in 2013-2014.

**Business.** Yeo & Yeo, P.C. receives professional audit services per its March 31, 2015 proposal, not to exceed $48,650 for 2014-2015, $50,400.00 for 2015-2016 and $52,150.00 for 2016-2017 from the General Fund, reviewed by Trustee Wendy Underwood, Rick West and Stephanie Maynard. Nova Environmental receives environmental testing for $42,920.00; SimplexGrinnell video surveillance for $325,507.00 off the Troy Police Department contract; Apple, Inc. 3,800 iPad Air tablets for $1,437,196.00 via the TRIG Statewide Purchasing Online Tool; CDWG 3,800 iPad covers for $87,400.00 via the AEPA contract; SEHI, Inc. Tripp-Lite power supplies for $37,787.41 via the REMC contract; ThermalNetics Troy High mechanical equipment for $327,500.00; and CDWG 2,400 Airwatch MDM licenses for $53,088.00 via NJPA, charged to the 2014-2015 General Fund. Boulan Park and Larson mechanical, electrical and site work totals $4,642,337.00 -- Advanced Building Group $232,000.00, Ecker Mechanical $2,446,257.00, Metro Electric $1,216,000.00, Nagle Paving $748,080.00. An April 27, 2015 letter from Convergent Technology Partners of Flint, signed by John C. Foster, RCDD, President and Kristie Young, Director of Technology, recommends a total award of $1,940,978.41.

**Oakland Schools budgets (8.J, 8.K).** Presented by Rick West under Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624), effective 2004. Annual property tax collection declined 23.4% from FY 2008 to FY 2015, a cumulative $244.4 million and an estimated $290.5 million through FY16, against an FY 2008 base-year levy of $216.9 million and an expected FY 2016 levy of $170.8 million. FY16 assumptions: 2.75% property tax increase, .3% personal property tax loss, possible Headlee rollback, QSCB interest subsidy reduced 7.2%; 1% pay increase, 25.91% retirement rate under MPSERS reform, average 15% employee health premium contribution under the hard cap. Total revenue $292.2 million -- property tax $170.8 million (58%), new grant award funding $74.3 million (25%), other local $23.4 million (8%), state $10.4 million (3%), other financing sources $8.0 million (3%), estimated grant carryover $5.3 million (3%). Total expenditures $300.0 million -- transfers to LEAs and other funds $132.6 million (44.2%), grant-related $79.5 million (26.5%), personnel $61.0 million (20.3%), purchased services, supplies, dues and fees $19.2 million (6.4%), debt service $4.0 million (1.3%), capital outlay and other $2.6 million (0.9%), utilities $1.1 million (0.4%). The General Education Fund forecast for 2015-16 shows $25.1 million revenue, $25.6 million expenditures, a $.5 million deficit and a $3.4 million ending unassigned fund balance at 13.4% of expenditures. Fiscal Year 2016 special education support totals $115,482,000: PA-18 base distribution $112,522,000, start-up contingency $500,000, Section 24 subsidy and other $100,000, group homes $1,910,000, Havenwyck $150,000, assistive technology equipment $300,000; the PA-18 base distribution increased $2.3M from FY15 while overall distribution decreases by $342K. Special education 2015-16 shows $133.0 million revenue, $133.3 million expenditures and a $2.5 million total ending fund balance; Career Focused Education shows $34.0 million revenue, $35.8 million expenditures, a $1.8 million deficit and a $3.5 million restricted ending fund balance at 9.7% of expenditures. Item 8.K resolves support solely for compliance with Section 624, forwarded no later than June 1, 2015 under the Open Meetings Act, 1976 PA 267.

**Other.** Ron Curtis, Senior Project Manager, Barton Malow, presents the 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update prepared with TMP: Troy High classroom and storage additions about December 2015, Athens LGI renovation Spring 2015, Boulan Park and Larson office additions about December 2015; BP #14 Administration and Service Center roofing bids due May 13, 2015. The first reading of the board policy on Compensation and Expenses -- listed as B-2001 on the agenda and headed B-2002 in the item -- sets compensation at $100 per annum; adopted January 16, 1979, revised March 17, 1998 and April 15, 2003.
